memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: In accordance with the Lord's command to him, Joshua gave to Caleb son of Jephunneh a portion in Judah—Kiriath Arba, that is, Hebron. (Arba was the forefather of Anak.) From Hebron Caleb drove out the three Anakites—Sheshai, Ahiman and Talmai, the sons of Anak. From there he marched against the people living in Debir (formerly called Kiriath Sepher) - Josh 15:13-15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
We meet Caleb again. Having asked for the hill country full of giants, he now does exactly what he said he would: he drives out the three Anakites, the giants of Hebron, and marches on toward Debir. The man who trusted God wholeheartedly at eighty-five now backs up his faith with action. He does not merely claim the mountain; he climbs it and fights.

Caleb's story reminds us that real faith moves. He had believed God's promise for forty-five years, and now that belief takes the shape of marching against fortified cities and defeating the very giants that had once terrified an entire generation of spies. Faith that stays in the heart and never reaches the feet is not yet the full faith Caleb had. His conviction and his conduct matched.

There is deep encouragement in watching Caleb defeat the giants he once only trusted God about. The obstacles that loomed so large in the report of the ten fearful spies are, in the end, driven out by one faithful old man leaning on God. Our giants, too, are not as unbeatable as our fears insist. When we go forward trusting God and acting on that trust, strongholds fall. And the greatest giants — sin and death — have already been defeated by Christ, so that we face our battles from the ground of His victory (1 Cor 15:57).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Does your faith reach your feet, or does it stay only in your heart?
- What giant have you been trusting God about but not yet acting against?
- How does Christ's victory embolden you to face your own strongholds?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, give me the faith of Caleb that moves — not only believing Your promises but acting on them. Thank You that I face my giants from the ground of Christ's victory. Amen.
